description: We are a team of four master's students at the Université de Sherbrooke, specializing in Artificial Intelligence, Big Data, and Cybersecurity. Passionate about technology, space exploration, and innovation, we enjoy tackling complex challenges and developing creative solutions. Through the NASA Space Apps Challenge, we aim to combine our technical skills, explore new ideas, and build an innovative, AI-driven project using NASA's open data.
summary:
Project Space D.U.C.K is a retro-style exploration game that puts players in the boots of a duck astronaut on Mars. Starting inside an interactive spaceship, players plan a rover expedition, travel from base to a sampling site, collect a scientific sample, and bring it home.

Along the way, eight minigames challenge players to manage rover problems, respond to changing winds, and protect samples from contamination. Route choices and player actions affect mission resources and sample quality, making each expedition a balance between exploration and responsible science.

Built with JavaScript and Phaser 3, the game combines NASA terrain, imagery, and environmental data with clearly identified gameplay assumptions. Python scripts process the data and generate routes, connecting the adventure to real Mars exploration.

Our goal is to make planetary protection approachable through play. Players discover why reaching a destination is only part of a successful mission: preserving the scientific value of a sample matters just as much.
details:
Project Space D.U.C.K is an educational exploration game that turns planetary protection into a playable Mars mission. Players control a duck astronaut, leave an interactive spaceship hub, choose a rover route through Jezero Crater, collect a sample, and return it to base.

The mission combines route planning with eight short minigames involving wind, traction, temperature, power management, sample collection, drilling, sealing, and steering. During sample collection, changing winds carry particles from the astronaut toward the sample. Players must reposition themselves to limit contamination while completing the extraction.

The game connects these decisions to NASA resources. Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter CTX elevation and imagery products, obtained through NASA JPL Mars Trek, support the terrain map and route calculations. Published Perseverance MEDA observations inform environmental conditions, while Mastcam-Z imagery provides geological context. Measured information, computed values, and gameplay assumptions are distinguished: the contamination model is an educational simulation, not a validated prediction of human activity on Mars.

We developed the game using JavaScript and Phaser 3. Python scripts process terrain data and calculate routes using A* pathfinding. HTML and CSS support browser delivery, and Electron packages the game as a standalone Windows executable.

Our creative approach combines a retro visual style, a memorable astronaut character, an explorable spaceship menu, and short interactive challenges. Instead of only explaining contamination, we let players experience how their decisions affect sample quality.

The intended impact is to make planetary protection and scientific sampling more approachable for students and general audiences. Development focused on readable interfaces, clear controls, fair outcomes, smooth transitions, and balancing scientific context with enjoyable gameplay.

Team: Hassan Ismaili Alaoui, Hidaya Lakhder, and Adam Guerrouani.
